title: Service standards, honest selling and your customer list

say: Service standards, honest selling and your customer list.
This is the video for module 3 of Customer Relations and Sales.
Without written standards, service depends on mood: excellent when you are rested, poor when you are tired. Customers notice the bad days most.

panel.heading: Good service on your busiest day
items: Service should not depend on your mood
Honest claims keep customers and keep you lawful
A written list shows who buys and who went quiet

say: Honest selling is not weak selling. Customers who trust you return and recommend you.

say: A service standard is a clear promise about how you treat customers, written down so you and any helper can keep it. Reply quickly is not a standard, because you cannot check it.

panel.heading: Vague intention or clear standard?
right: Repeat every order back in writing
Check in within 2 days of delivery

say: Reply to every message within 1 hour, 8am to 7pm, is a standard. You can check whether you did it.
Choose promises you can keep on your busiest day, not your best day. A smaller promise kept is better than a big promise broken.

say: Nigeria's consumer protection law expects accurate information and honest claims. First, never say a cream, tea or soap cures a disease. That is a medical claim, and NAFDAC rules are strict.

panel.heading: Claims to avoid
items: Cure claims: never say it cures a disease
False origin: original or imported, unless true
Fake scarcity: only 2 left, when untrue
Edited or borrowed photos
Fake reviews and hidden charges

say: Do not call a product original or imported unless you are sure it is true.

say: Before you post any sales message, ask four questions. Is it true? Can you prove every claim?

panel.heading: The four-question ethics test
items: Is it true? Can you prove every claim?
Is it fair? Would you treat your mother this way?
Would you say it in public?
Will she still be happy next month?

say: Is it fair? Would you be happy if a seller treated your mother this way?

panel.heading: The four-question ethics test
items: Is it true? Can you prove every claim?

Would you say it in public?

say: Would you say it in public, in front of your whole church or market association?

panel.rule: Your list is personal data. Keep it private and locked.

say: Here is how the list guides you. Ada keeps a Google Sheet.
In March she recorded 30 orders worth 285,000 naira.
Her average order is 285,000 divided by 30, which is 9,500 naira.
Of 22 customers, 14 had bought before. And she finds 6 regulars who have not bought in over 8 weeks. She sends each a personal check-in, and two of them reorder within the week.
To remember. A standard is a specific promise you can check, so review it every week. Never make cure claims, fake scarcity or fake reviews. Use the four-question test.
And each month, count your repeat customers, your average order and your quiet customers.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Standards are specific promises you can check
Review your standards every week
No cure claims, fake scarcity or fake reviews
True, fair, public, happy next month
Count repeat, average and quiet customers monthly

say: Your turn. Write five service standards and keep a tally for one week. Check five of your recent posts and rewrite any that fail the test. Start your customer list with at least 10 customers, and mark three for a follow-up this week.
